governing_question: After D17 retained bounded combined FMC candidacy and D18 showed that one natural contact-event route was not reached, did D11 omit a materially distinct published reduction family that should be tested before inventing further custom FMC/ROM architectures?

historical_governance.D11_statement: D11 remains the historical reviewed-set decision. D19 expands the reviewed set with GARTO/LGAR evidence that was not included there.

primary_sources.citation: Lai, Ogden, Steinke & Talbot (2015), An efficient and guaranteed stable numerical method for continuous modeling of infiltration and redistribution with a shallow dynamic water table, Water Resources Research 51, 1514-1528.
Ogden et al. (2015), A new general 1-D vadose zone flow solution method, Water Resources Research 51, 4282-4300.
La Follette, Ogden & Jan (2023), Layered Green and Ampt Infiltration With Redistribution, Water Resources Research 59.

statements: Combines GAR redistribution with selected Talbot-Ogden concepts rather than discretizing the complete surface moisture-content domain into ~200 finite-water-content states.
Represents a limited number of explicit surface wetting fronts; the published simulations set maximum surface-front capacity N=10 and observed at most three active surface fronts.
Allows all active surface wetting fronts to infiltrate, merges overshooting surface fronts conservatively, and uses a redistribution ODE for rainfall below Ks.
Adds capillary groundwater fronts and a dynamic-water-table ODE; a surface front that touches a groundwater front becomes groundwater.
Supports infiltration-excess and saturation-excess behavior and was tested with multiple rainfall pulses, runoff, shallow fixed water tables and a rising water table.
Guaranteed mass conservation and numerical stability are part of the published method identity.
GARTO_scientific_identity.state_dimension_note: Surface state is materially lower-order than the 200-bin FMC route. The groundwater branch still uses a front/bin discretization whose exact published operational count must be reconciled before a faithful SWAP comparator; the paper notes that shallow-water-table behavior can be smoothed by increasing groundwater bins.
GARTO_scientific_identity.ET_note: The paper states ET could be represented by withdrawing water from the right-most wetting front at root-zone depth, but does not test ET in the reported study. This is not SWAP root-uptake authority.

hydraulic_mapping.B01_rule: Use the existing B01 Van Genuchten/Mualem functions directly and evaluate the effective capillary-drive integral numerically. Do not fit/convert B01 to Brooks-Corey merely to reproduce the paper.
hydraulic_mapping.reason: The primary paper explicitly states that Van Genuchten can be used, with numerical integration of effective capillary drive or parameter conversion; numerical integration avoids introducing a new soil-parameter calibration.

external_evidence.accuracy_scope: External GARTO-vs-FUCG-Richards evidence only; not SWAP acceptance thresholds.

moving_water_table.condition: four coarser soils, water table rising at 5 cm/h, surface rainfall/runoff, soil becoming saturated then draining
moving_water_table.finding: GARTO and FUCG Richards were qualitatively similar, with reported soil-dependent differences.

shallow_water_table_tradeoff.statement: Published cumulative-infiltration discrepancy grows as the water table approaches the surface.

runtime.hardware_context: CentOS Linux 6.5, 3.4 GHz Intel i7; external study only

strengths: continuous multi-event infiltration in an arbitrary number of soil layers
blockers_for_current_dynamic_WT_question: primary LGAR derivation explicitly assumes no influence of groundwater table on soil moisture
application envelope emphasizes arid/semi-arid conditions where cumulative PET exceeds cumulative precipitation

HydPy_GARTO.relevance: HydPy documents a GARTO implementation checked against original C source supplied by two GARTO authors.
HydPy_GARTO.caveat: HydPy explicitly documents differences and generally assumes hydrostatic groundwater rather than the complete dynamic-groundwater GARTO method.

open_boundaries: contact/merge hydrology not yet reached in D18

GARTO.potential_advantage: substantially lower surface-state complexity and strong external moving-WT/runtime precedent
open_boundaries: B01 Van Genuchten capillary-drive numerical integration qualification

D20_authority.title: Literature-faithful GARTO equation/source benchmark and bounded B01 comparator
stage1_source_equation_authority: Transcribe and test GARTO equations 6, 8, 9, 10 and effective capillary-drive relation from the primary source.
Reconcile original/source-code semantics where available, especially wetting-front ordering, surface-water allocation, merge ordering and groundwater-front/bin representation.
Determine and freeze the groundwater discretization used for a published shallow/moving-water-table benchmark before SWAP evidence.
Freeze maximum surface wetting fronts N=10 and process time step 10 s from the published study for the first faithful benchmark.
No SWAP trajectory may be used in Stage 1.
stage2_published_benchmark: Reproduce at least one primary-source GARTO benchmark with Brooks-Corey parameters before B01 mapping.
Include a shallow or rising-water-table case, not only deep infiltration.
Verify exact/explicit mass closure, front ordering, surface/groundwater contact behavior and benchmark direction/magnitude against published evidence.
Any ambiguity in groundwater bins or moving-water-table update is a blocker, not a tuning invitation.
stage3_B01_if_and_only_if_stage2_passes: effective capillary drive by frozen numerical integration of B01 constitutive law; no Brooks-Corey fitting
surface flux and water-table boundary only within reconciled GARTO authority
FMC D17 retained as an architecture comparator where envelopes overlap
development evidence only; no application acceptance
D20_authority.performance_boundary: Published FUCG speedups are motivation only. No SWAP5 speed claim until same-runtime implementation and admitted performance host exist.
